description: Global Trade Alert is a database of government policy interventions that affect international trade, covering trade and industrial policy changes announced by governments, each dated by announcement. It is an initiative of the St. Gallen Endowment for Prosperity through Trade (SGEPT), supported by the University of St. Gallen and the Schmidheiny Foundation, launched in 2009 and covering measures since the 2008 financial crisis. Coverage is global, with entries updated continuously; announcements dated September 2026 were on the home page at access. Data can be extracted in the Data Center, pulled through an API or Power BI, or followed through notification services; content is under CC BY-NC 4.0 unless stated otherwise, free for non-commercial users, with commercial licences by geography and policy package. Caveats: coverage depends on what the team can document, and classification of measures involves judgement. For simulation it provides export restrictions and other shocks for trade network and supply chain resilience models, for example fertiliser, food or critical mineral export bans. It is related to the WITS record in this catalogue, which gives the trade flows these measures affect.
